Its data is not a baseline for this new workload version.

## Workload version 2 and correctness

Eight distinct authored configs import the same complete `support.ts` declarations. Every App starts at version 1 with the already queried `totals.invoiceTotal` member assigned a string while its imported factory declares a number. The authored whole diagnostic oracle is one 2322 packet, including its full message/range/source/severity. Version 3 switches the imported factory to `makeStringTotals`; the same assignment is then legal and the whole diagnostic packet must be empty. No unused error-only binding or extra query is added. The whole hover changes from number to string, and the existing complete completion item/wrapper laws remain. This expected 2322 range is prepared source-only; actual provider execution has not yet validated the new input.

Each session opens contexts sequentially and records milestones at 1, 4 and 8 qualified targets. It sends all eight didClose notifications, waits the original 250 ms, samples `closed`, reopens all eight with version 3, qualifies every repair and samples `reopened8`. Every query/publication/resource error is retained; later targets and milestones keep the existing failure-preservation behavior. All four attempts and their raw results remain in the campaign before the final verdict. No failed attempt is retried or trimmed.

The 250 ms is a fixed observation interval, **not** a close acknowledgment, eviction proof or native quiescence barrier. The primary context may never initialize; held old leases/entered workers may outlive close. No fixed child-process count, two-process target, PID-to-config map or forced shutdown is imposed. Actual selected config/source owner facts are joined only through the retained trace records; unavailable or conflicting authority fails the existing coverage guard.

The native hover Markdown has one newline after the closing code fence, as established by the already held exact primary `hover.go` source. No new resolve RPC is introduced. These memory queries do not promote the old unresolved opaque projection to independent authority.

## Measurement and custody

Both roles are built freshly with `cargo build --release -p vize`, default features, opt level 3 and no profiling/micro-profiling. Cargo JSON binds the actual CLI, Maestro native feature and all seven SDK beta4 artifacts. The ten declaration files, package/generator inputs, source paths, original LSP harness and physical provider `@typescript/typescript-linux-x64@7.0.2` are recorded before/after. The FIRST release CLI is protected outside the evidence directory and restored before each attempt. No library tests are repeated or given same-image CLI credit. The existing shipping receipt adapter remains byte-exact; no original tracked benchmark is changed or invoked by this memory-only workload.

RSS sampling retains the original 50 ms request interval, actual gaps and every owned process birth. Memory safety remains root **2048 MiB**, tree **8192 MiB**, **32 processes**. These limits are separate from the original ordinary root 256/tree 512/process 4 gate, whose existing failures remain failures. Known-owned stat access denial is a coverage failure. Untimed PSS and executable identity reads occur at the five fixed milestones and remain sequential best-effort reads, not atomic snapshots.

Report the actual root and descendant components at the **same recorded tree-peak row**. Do not sum independent root and descendant maxima. PID/birth joins for sequential PSS/identity reads require adjacent RSS identity evidence; otherwise label them UNJOINED. The trace-on observer has overhead, so no latency headline, native allocation-volume theorem, ordinary memory repair or general memory win follows from it. There are only two cohorts per source; retain every value and outlier.

## Output and bounded forecast

Expected campaign output is two fresh build custody directories and four attempt directories, each containing terminal exit/raw stdout/stderr, before/after identities, workload outcome, memory JSON/events/RSS and one closed three-stream LSP capture plus observation metadata. All original per-stream/event/RSS caps and quota refusals remain; truncation cannot become complete coverage. Actual archive metadata must be checked before transport. A planning estimate is 3–8 MiB compressed and 15–35 MiB expanded based on the old held captures; it is not a new artifact cap or guarantee. The fixed per-stream caps permit larger failures. No ELF, provider image, Cargo target or SDK archive is uploaded. Disk forecast and the existing 1 GiB free-space floor remain transport prerequisites.

Pure controls and strict TypeScript validate only controller laws. They provide no Rust, native, measured B/C or release qualification. Publication and one existing-frontdoor execution remain held for final source and functional closure plus finite source review.
